overview.definition: RDK-B (Reference Design Kit – Broadband) is an open-source, modular, operator-grade middleware platform providing a standardized software stack for broadband residential and business devices. RDKB components are open-sourced, vendor-independent, actively maintained, and each represented by one or more GitHub repositories.
overview.intro: RDK-B sits between the hardware SoC/BSP layer and the operator's cloud management systems, providing a rich set of pre-integrated components for Wi-Fi, routing, diagnostics, telemetry, device management, IoT, and application containerization. Its HAL abstraction model means that a single software stack can run on radically different SoC platforms. Typically, each RDKB component contains a logical grouping of related features, and this modular approach allows software developers to select the set of high-level features required for each software build.

governance_standards.name: Component modularity and organization
governance_standards.requirement: New or refactored software components MUST contain only software that implements a grouping of similar features. This design helps to ensure that the component may be added to a software build only when that feature set is needed. Software to implement other unrelated features MUST NOT be included in the component. The software source code, build recipes, unit test mechanisms and documentation for a component SHOULD be contained in a single software repo. If any of this is contained in more than one repo, the documentation in each repo must reference all other software repos containing any of this information for the component. Distro Flags SHOULD be implemented for all sub-features that may not be required for all markets or operators.

governance_standards.name: Component IPC Guidelines
governance_standards.requirement: RBUS APIs are the authoritative interface for RDKB component to component interprocess communications (IPC). All new software contributions to existing and new components MUST exclusively use RBUS APIs for IPC with other RDKB components. Contributions to both existing and new components MUST be scanned using a common RDK static analysis tool to compare with previous versions of the component (if any) to ensure that no new usage of older IPC mechanisms is added, including syseventd, DMCLI or CCSP APIs.

governance_standards.name: Component Build-Time Dependency Policy
governance_standards.requirement: Mandatory architecture review MUST be conducted for all new inter-component build-time dependencies. RDKB components MUST NOT have build-time dependencies with other RDKB components that are optional or N/A for any software profile(s). Components MAY have build-time dependencies with Common Core Components.

governance_standards.name: Component Run-Time Dependency Policy
governance_standards.requirement: Mandatory architecture review MUST be conducted for all new inter-component run-time dependencies. RDKB components MAY access/consume data model elements implemented in other components or implemented in downloaded apps. This MAY include data model elements implemented in components that are optional or N/A for any profile. Components MUST NOT have hard (inflexible) run-time dependencies on these data model elements. If data model element(s) are not available, the accessing/consuming component MUST dynamically adapt to use only the data model elements and capabilities that are available at runtime. Components that attempt to access/consume data models that are unavailable MUST NOT stall, crash or fail to provide features unrelated to the missing data model elements.

governance_standards.name: Component Unit Testing Requirements
governance_standards.requirement: All new components MUST ship with isolated unit tests requiring no external dependencies. HAL interfaces must have rdkb-halif-test-* suite before being declared stable. Test coverage metrics MUST be published per release. Testing must auto-discover the supported data model elements (including event and method usage) and auto-create a document of the supported data model elements when each feature flag is enabled. This document MUST (at a minimum) list all data model names provided in the component and which APIs are supported for each data model (set, get, add instance, delete instance, subscribe to event, un-subscribe, method invoke).

governance_standards.name: Data Model Documentation Standards
governance_standards.requirement: Data Model documentation MUST be sufficient to enable other developers/testers/system integrators to understand how to use each data model element. When a software contribution is received that updates an existing component or creates a new component, the contribution MUST contain detailed documentation of any new data models and changes to older data models. This MUST include the data model name, the supported RBUS APIs (examples: Set, Get, Add Instance, Subscribe, Unsubscribe, Method Invoke,

governance_standards.name: Data Model Standards (TR-181)
governance_standards.requirement: Data models used in RDKB software contributions SHOULD follow the TR-181 standard when possible. Software contributions that use a data model name previously documented in the TR-181 standard MUST fully comply with the most recent TR-181 documentation for that name. If the most recent TR181 standard does not provide a data model name with the desired new functionality or the software contribution does not fully comply with how TR-181 standard describes how an existing name is used, then a new data model name MAY be created. New data model names MUST use the TR-181 organization and hierarchy when possible. New data model names MUST comply with the applicable extension format for non-standard names. New data model names SHOULD use the format: <existing TR-181 object hierarchy>.X_RDK-<new name>.

governance_standards.name: HAL Documentation Standards
governance_standards.requirement: Each HAL interface must have a published interface specification document.

governance_standards.name: Interface Versioning & Backward Compatibility
governance_standards.requirement: All components and HAL interface MUST follow semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Large functional changes and any change that is not backward compatible MUST increment the MAJOR version. Small planned features additions or bug fixes SHOULD increment the MINOR version. Unplanned bug fixes SHOULD increment the PATCH version. Deprecated interfaces SHOULD remain supported a minimum of two release cycles before removal.

governance_standards.name: Telemetry & Observability Standards
governance_standards.requirement: Components MUST emit logs conforming to the RDK-B common logging format. Critical state transitions SHOULD publish RBUS events and/or provide status properties that can be read by other RBUS components. .

governance_standards.name: Build & Packaging Standards (Yocto/OE)
governance_standards.requirement: Components MUST build cleanly under the supported Yocto release with no layer dependency cycles. Recipes MUST declare explicit LICENSE and SPDX identifiers. Distro flags MUST gate all profile-specific or optional features.

governance_standards.name: Error Handling & Resilience Standards
governance_standards.requirement: Components MUST use defined RBUS error codes, not custom/undocumented codes. Crash-prone components MUST integrate with systemd watchdog and support clean restart without state corruption. Core dumps MUST be captured via the CrashUpload framework.

governance_standards.name: Naming & Repository Conventions
governance_standards.requirement: Component repos MUST follow the rdkb-<component> convention. New components MUST follow the Rdk* prefix and <Function> HAL suffix conventions already established in the architecture. Branch naming aligns with governance branch policy (7.2.12).

governance_standards.name: Code Quality & Static Analysis Standards
governance_standards.requirement: New C/C++ components MUST pass static analysis (cppcheck/Coverity) with zero high-severity findings before merge. Coding style MUST conform to the published RDK-B style guide. Memory safety tooling (ASan/Valgrind) runs in CI for native builds.

governance_standards.name: Northbound Protocol Onboarding
governance_standards.requirement: Any new remote-management protocol (beyond TR-369/TR-069/WebPA/Webconfig/SNMP/DAC/SSH) MUST be supported with a new Protocol Adapter component designed to abstract that protocol and allow the protocol to transparently send corresponding messages to other components using RBUS APIs. New protocols MUST NOT reach into RDKB components directly.

governance_standards.name: WAN Technology Onboarding
governance_standards.requirement: A new WAN access technology MUST integrate through RdkWanManager plus a technology-specific manager/agent (following the GPON/xDSL/Cellular/Docsis/EPON pattern); bespoke managers outside this pattern require architecture review.

governance_standards.name: Edge AI / ML Integration Standards*
governance_standards.requirement: AI/ML inference components MUST use vendor-neutral model formats (ONNX/RKNN), decoupled from any single NPU vendor SDK. Inference latency and resource budgets documented per model. Versioning/rollback supported for production deployment. Layer placement (dedicated color-coded layer vs folded into other RDKB layers) still needs a decision before this is fully ready.

governance_standards.name: Integration of differentiating or proprietary software Third-Party Component Integration & HAL Extension Standards
governance_standards.requirement: Developers and System Integrators that desire to add differentiation or proprietary software on top of RDKB open source should follow one of two paths: 1) New differentiating or proprietary software that is hardware independent SHOULD use the existing TR-181 data models already supported by RDKB in order to control, optimize or extend RDKB features where possible. If new code needs to be added to the RDKB open source software to provide basic enabling features, then new data models to support this SHOULD be contributed to the RDKB community. This MAY be done while excluding differentiating or proprietary software by packaging that software in components that are NOT open sourced to the community. 2) New differentiating or proprietary software that is hardware dependent may be added in the vendor layer. This software MUST support RDK HAL API definitions. If HAL APIs need to be modified or extended, vendor MUST work with the RDK community to make these changes. This allows vendors to differentiate within the vendor layer while keeping a c ommon interface to the vendor layer.

governance_standards.name: IPC Mechanism Selection
governance_standards.requirement: RBUS is the default and only sanctioned IPC for new RDKB components. D-Bus is permitted only for legacy/vendor OSS that natively requires it (e.g. ModemManager), bridged into RBUS rather than consumed directly. USP/UDS is reserved for the USP Agent↔Controller boundary only. Downloaded Apps may use USP/UDS provided that a USP/UDS API Gateway converts these messages to RBUS. Any other IPC requires architecture review with documented justification.

governance_standards.name: Eventing Standards
governance_standards.requirement: State-change events SHOULD be published via RBUS event/subscribe, not polling Event payloads that contain a value SHOULD carry both updated parameter/value and the previous parameter/value. High-frequency events (>1/sec) SHOULD be rate-limited or coalesced at the publisher unless typical use cases require all high frequency events to be published

governance_standards.name: Storage & Persistence Standards
governance_standards.requirement: Data-model-backed parameters requiring persistence SHOULD use PSM or a new common method defined in the future. Structured local storage (logs, model artifacts) MUST use a defined path with documented size quotas with no writes to rootfs.

governance_standards.name: Footprint / CPU / RAM Budget
governance_standards.requirement: Every new component MUST document typical RAM, peak RAM, and flash footprint targets at design review, scoped to its device profile tier. Regressions beyond an agreed threshold versus prior release require architecture sign-off. Lower-tier profiles MUST never silently inherit other-profile footprint assumptions.

governance_standards.name: system()/Shell-out Usage
governance_standards.requirement: Calling system()/popen() from C/C++ daemons is discouraged by default; native library calls are preferred. Where unavoidable, the call MUST check return codes, sanitize interpolated input against shell injection, and never runs in a signal handler or high-frequency loop.

governance_standards.name: OSS Usage Standards
governance_standards.requirement: OSS dependencies come from the sanctioned Linux OSS layer list; new dependencies require review for license compatibility, CVE history, and maintenance activity. RDK-B wraps OSS via a thin adapter rather than embedding internals directly. Forking OSS instead of upstreaming requires approval plus a reconciliation plan.

governance_standards.name: @When to Use HAL
governance_standards.requirement: Any interaction with vendor/SoC-specific hardware or firmware MUST pass through a published HAL; direct vendor SDK calls MUST NOT be used.. A HAL is required only where behavior differs across silicon vendors — platform-independent behavior belongs in Linux OSS or a native component.

governance_standards.name: No RDK-B IPC Within vendor layer
governance_standards.requirement: Vendor layer HAL implementations MUST NOT contain TR-181/data-model awareness, RBUS usage or sysevent/syscfg calls.

governance_standards.name: Direct Kernel Interaction
governance_standards.requirement: Components talk to the kernel directly (syscalls, sysfs, procfs) only for OS-level facilities with no existing HAL/OSS abstraction. Any kernel interface used by more than one component is wrapped in a shared internal library, not duplicated. New kernel module/driver dependencies require platform-layer governance review (7.2.6).

governance_standards.name: Netlink vs Other Kernel Interfaces
governance_standards.requirement: Netlink is preferred for asynchronous kernel notifications (link state, routing, neighbor changes); polling sysfs/procfs where a netlink equivalent exists is prohibited. ioctl is permitted only for legacy drivers with no netlink support, isolated behind a HAL/adapter.

governance_standards.name: C/C++ Coding Anti-Patterns
governance_standards.requirement: Blocking I/O MUST NOT occur on a component's main RBUS event-handling thread. strcpy/sprintf and unbounded buffers for variable-length input MUST NOT be used in favor of bounded equivalents; malloc return values MUST always be checked and an error must be logged and returned to higher level software Global mutable state shared across translation units is prohibited except through a documented, lock-protected accessor.

governance_standards.name: Sysevent Usage Standards
governance_standards.requirement: Sysevent usage is expected to be deprecated over time. New software contributions MUST NOT add to sysevent usage or add any new sysevent keys.

governance_standards.name: Scripting Usage Standards
governance_standards.requirement: Shell scripts MAY be used for one-shot boot/init orchestration and MUST NOT be used for long running stateful logic. Interpreted languages are discouraged on memory/flash-constrained profiles unless explicitly justified — native C/C++ or RUST SHOULD be used

governance_standards.name: Calling C/C++ from Scripts
governance_standards.requirement: Scripts MUST call into native functionality via the component's published data model interface using rbuscli or RBUS APIs. Scripts MUST NOT link against internal .so symbols outside a published API. Scripts MUST NOT parse internal binary log/state formats.

governance_standards.name: RFC vs syscfg vs Build Flag
governance_standards.requirement: A features or behavior SHOULD use a data model property or method invocation for enable/disable if the feature or behavior needs remote, post-deployment toggling without a firmware push. An operator specific or device specific “Factory Default” value may be used at build time to control the default behavior of a feature. A feature or behavior that needs to be controlled at build time SHOULD use a Distro/build flag. Large features MAY be controlled at build time by the presence/absence of a software component in the build.

governance_standards.name: Threading & Concurrency Model
governance_standards.requirement: New daemons MUST default to a single-threaded event loop unless a specific workload justifies multi-threading. Where threads are used, lock ordering MUST be documented and mutexes MUST NOT be held across an RBUS call. There MUST NOT be unbounded thread spawning per request/connection.

governance_standards.name: Logging Level Standards
governance_standards.requirement: Components MUST use rdk_logger exclusively, never raw printf/syslog. ERROR is reserved for conditions requiring operator/telemetry attention; DEBUG/TRACE SHOULD be compiled out or runtime-gated in production builds.

governance_standards.name: Shared Library ABI Versioning
governance_standards.requirement: Any .so consumed by more than one component MUST follow symbol versioning

blocks.text: The purpose of RDKB Broadband governance is to ensure that every new component, enhancement, bug fix, interface change, and platform integration follows a common technical standard before it is accepted into the RDK-B codebase. The governance process must ensure:
Generic implementation suitable for community adoption
Test evidence availability for every change
Controlled release inclusion and traceability No code change should be merged into a RDKB branch unless architecture, interface, dependency, test, and release expectations are satisfied.
HAL, Linux OSS, or platform-layer interaction
Every change must be classified before development starts.

A new component is any new software contribution that creates a new RDKB open source repo or collection of repos that provides new features, services or other software to be included in RDKB open source. New components SHOULD be organized so that operators can include this software only when they need a particular set of new features or services. New components MUST be organized as a collection of logically similar features or services that may be included or excluded from a finished software build as a group New components MUST NOT be an unrelated collection of features or services. Examples:
New RDK-B open source software that provides a logical group of features or services that may be compiled and used as part of a monolithic software image
New RDKB open source software that provides a logical group of features or services that may be compiled and used as a downloaded app.

New RDKB open source software that provides a logical group of features or services that may contain multiple build recipes so that can optionally be compiled and built as part of a monolithic image or built as a downloaded app
An enhancement modifies or extends the features or services provided by an existing component without changing the basic ownership of the component. Examples:
New features or services inside existing component repositories
New data model parameter(s) provided by the component used for configuration, telemetry, eventing or method invocation.
Support for a modified HAL API
A bug fix corrects an existing defect without introducing new feature behavior. Examples:
Platform compatibility fix Bug fixes must be generic and community-aligned. Local hacks, platform-specific shortcuts, or hidden behavior under flags should not be accepted unless formally justified.
Before development starts, the contributor must create a design/review ticket with the following information.
A new component proposal must include:
Functional scope including a list of the features/services provided
Details on usage in all RDKB profiles. The proposal should indicate if this new component is required, optional or not applicable for each RDKB profile.

A list of all planned data model names to be provided by this component. This must include as much detail as possible regarding the feature and purpose of each data model and detailed syntax and usage information.

A list of all planned data model names to be consumed by this component (data model names that are provided by other components). Include how this component’s behavior is impacted if any of the components that provide these data models are not included in the software build.
A refactoring statement that lists any software or features that are currently or were previously in other components (if any).
Build-time dependency list of other RDKB components
Build-time dependency list of other open source software Runtime dependency list

List of schedule dependencies with other proposed changes (if any) Example if this new component is created due to refactoring of an existing component, this should reference the changes required in the other component(s) that have to be done at the same time. Telemetry impact
HAL APIs used (including open source implementations like NL80211)
Changes to data models provided by this component
Changes to data models consumed by this component and how the behavior of this component is impacted if any of the components that provide these data models are not included in the software build.
Dependency impact with other RDKB components
Dependency impact with non-RDK open-source dependencies
A list of HAL APIs that are updated or any new HAL APIs used by this component
A bug fix proposal must include:
Whether the fix is generic or platform-specific
Whether the issue exists in stable branch, rdk-next, or both
All new component contributions and major enhancements require architecture review before implementation or merge. Architecture review must validate:
Whether the component is required, optional or not applicable to each RDKB profile
Whether the component or change duplicates existing functionality
Whether the new component name is a good summary or label for its functionality. Don’t use names without meaning that make it hard to understand.
Whether the component or change is documented sufficiently for review
Whether the component or changes is hardware independent and properly abstracted from any hardware or vendor dependencies.
Whether the component or change meets the IPC guidelines

Whether the group of new features or services make sense to be in the proposed new or existing component from an operator perspective. (Is this a logical grouping of features or services that may be included/excluded from a software build)
Whether the component follows RDKB design principles
Whether the build time dependency model is acceptable
Whether the run-time dependency model is acceptable
Whether platform-specific logic is isolated correctly
Whether HAL/Linux OSS access is done through approved layers
Whether interfaces are stable and backward compatible
Whether the component can run across reference platforms
Whether the component is testable in CI and on hardware
Whether this software is covered by an acceptable software license approval is mandatory for:
Components must not directly embed board-specific logic inside RDKB implementations.to be aligned with HAL spec
An RDKB component should access platform functionality in the following order:
Platform-specific fallback only when formally approved
Use Linux OSS interfaces when the functionality is standard and portable. Examples:
standard systemd interaction where applicable Linux OSS usage must be validated across supported kernel versions and reference platforms.
A common vendor independent interface to vendor specific drivers or low-level software is required.
Radio, switch, PHY, WAN, LAN, or hardware diagnostics behavior is not portable through standard Linux APIs HAL usage must follow these rules:
HAL must not expose vendor-private implementation details
HAL header must be reviewed before implementation
HAL failure handling must be defined
Stub/reference implementation must be available where possible
Component must degrade gracefully if capability is not supported

Direct vendor SDK/API calls make RDKB open source software vendor dependent and violate the spirit and intent of RDKB. Direct vendor SDK/API calls inside RDKB component code are not allowed unless formally approved.
Every component must declare and justify:
Package dependencies New dependencies must be reviewed for:
Impact on minimal profile builds No new mandatory dependency should be added to RDKB components unless it is required for generic broadband functionality.
Run local build and unit tests
Merge only after sanity pass (including a comparison with run-time data model auto-discovery)
Run unit, functional, and regression tests
Complete RTAB approval if component behavior changes
Merge after sanity pass (including a comparison with run-time data model auto-discovery)
Include in release notes if user-visible or interface-impacting
Add details of how this was fixed to the defect ticket
Merge only after sanity pass (including a comparison with run-time data model auto-discovery)
Decide whether fix is needed in stable branch, rdk-next, or both
Testing is mandatory for every new component, enhancement, and bug fix. No code change should be merged if required sanity testing fails.
Each change must be evaluated against the following test categories. Build Validation
Static build dependency check Unit Testing
Sysevent scan to verify no new sysevent usage
Mock HAL test if HAL is involved Functional Testing
CLI/API validation where applicable Integration Testing
API authentication/authorization where applicable Stability Testing
Data Model run-time auto-discovery to document usage
Sysevent scan to verify no new sysevent usage
Data Model run-time auto-discovery to document usage
Sysevent scan to verify no new sysevent usage
Data Model run-time auto-discovery to document usage
Sysevent scan to verify no new sysevent usage
Each change must define which platforms were tested and why.
At minimum, RDK-B component changes should be validated on:
Emulated or CI platform where available Example platform categories:
Raspberry Pi or generic reference platform
Banana Pi R4 / Filogic / active broadband reference hardware
Vendor platform if the change is hardware-specific
Test on hardware platform when the change impacts:
System service behavior Test on CI/emulated platform when the change impacts:
Validate that generic platforms are not broken
Isolate platform logic outside the RDKB components when possible
Provide fallback behavior for unsupported capability
Every change must state which branch/build was validated.

technical_governance_process.title: Stable Working Branches (one branch for each supported LTS release)

blocks.text: Backport candidates Replace the change on other supported LTS branches where applicable
Validate release need on target stable branches if required
Backport only after fix/feature is stable and approved For bug fixes:
Validate on the branch where issue was found
Validate on rdk-next if the code exists there
Validate backport branches if release requires it
All reviews must be tracked using:
Architecture review record for new RDKB component or major change
Review record for applicable changes or breaking changes
Architecture owner for new component or major enhancement
HAL owner if HAL is impacted
RTAB for major RDKB component or breaking interface changes
Logs are useful but not excessive
Data Models used for telemetry are meaningful
A change can be merged only when all applicable conditions are met.
Required sanity tests passed including data model run-time auto-discovery
Rollback plan documented for high-risk changes
Code must not be merged if:
Functional test failure has no root cause
Change is hidden under a flag without justification
Fix is platform-specific but placed in RDKB Component generic code
Release engineer cannot confirm primary expectation is met
All test results must be attached to the ticket or PR. Evidence must include:
Pass/fail status for each test case
Component level data model auto-discovery list
Tester name or automation job link
Deviations or exceptions For every failed functional test:
A development ticket must be created
Root cause analysis must be provided
Fix must be generic enough for community alignment
Release impact must be assessed No release-bound change should be accepted with unexplained failures.
A change can be included in release only when:
Feature/bug ticket is closed or release-approved
PR is merged into correct branch
Release engineer confirms primary expectation is met
Release notes are updated if needed
Data model changes from run-time auto-discovery

Changes should be released based on classification: New Component Release in planned major/minor release after full validation. Enhancement Release in planned feature release unless it is required for a committed operator/customer milestone. Bug Fix Release in next maintenance release or patch release depending on severity. Critical/Security Fix Release through expedited patch process after mandatory validation and approval.
No code change should be accepted under a flag unless truly required. Flags are allowed only when at least one of the following is true:
Feature is not required for all operators or markets
Feature consumes large amounts of memory and may not be suitable for all devices
Feature consumes large amounts of CPU and may not be suitable for all devices
Feature is not applicable for some RDKB profiles when other features in the same component are applicable
Platform capability is not universally available
Backward compatibility requires coexistence Flags are not allowed for:
Bypassing community alignment Every flag must have:
Test coverage for enabled and disabled modes

technical_governance_process.title: Reference Platform and Community Contribution Rules

blocks.text: All community contributions and Reference Platform team changes must be validated before merge. Required expectations:
Code must build on reference platform
No reference-only assumption should enter RDKB Components
Platform-specific changes must remain in platform layer
Test evidence must be available in ticket/PR
RDK Broadband changes must be generic, portable, testable, and community aligned. No code change should be merged or released unless:
The implementation aligns with RDK-B architecture principles

The purpose of Component Governance is to ensure that every RDK-B component has a defined owner, a known lifecycle state, a health baseline, and a clear exit path. While Section 7.2 governs how changes are introduced and validated, Section 7.3 governs what happens to a component across its entire life — from registration through active maintenance to deprecation and removal. Component governance must ensure:
Every RDK-B component has a registered owner at all times
Component lifecycle state is known and current
Orphaned or unhealthy components are identified and resolved
Deprecated components have a defined migration path
HAL contracts and TR-181 parameters are transferred cleanly when components change state
Community contributors and operators have visibility into component health and roadmap
Every component accepted into RDK-B must be registered in the Component Registry at merge time. The registry is the authoritative record of all active, deprecated, and removed components.
Classification for each RDKB profile (CORE / Required / Optional / Not Applicable)
Current lifecycle state (Active / Stable / Deprecated / Removed)
Provided TR-181 data model provided by the component with list of names, syntax and usage details for each name
List of dependent non-RDKB open source components
Registry must be updated at every release
Any change to owner, state, or interfaces must trigger a registry update
RTAB is responsible for registry accuracy
Registry must be publicly accessible to the RDK community
Every RDK-B component must be in exactly one lifecycle state at all times.

rows: Active
Component is under active development and maintenance. New features, enhancements, and bug fixes are accepted. Full governance process applies.
Stable
Component interface is frozen. Only critical bug fixes and security fixes are accepted. No new features. HAL contract is locked.
Deprecated
Component is scheduled for removal. No new features or enhancements accepted. Critical security fixes only. Migration path is defined and published.
Removed
Component is no longer part of RDK-B. Repository archived. No changes accepted.

blocks.text: Active → Stable: Requires architecture owner approval. Interface freeze declared. HAL contract version locked.
Stable → Deprecated: Requires RTAB approval. Migration path must be defined before transition.
Deprecated → Removed: Requires RTAB approval. Migration path must be confirmed complete. Operator notification period must have elapsed.
Any State → Active: Requires RTAB approval if previously Stable or Deprecated.
Every RDK-B component must have a defined primary owner and a secondary owner at all times.
The primary owner is responsible for:
Review and approval of all PRs touching the component
Representing the component in RTAB and architecture reviews
Defining the migration plan if deprecation is required
When a primary owner is no longer available:
Secondary owner automatically assumes primary responsibility
A new primary/secondary owner must be nominated within one release cycle
If no secondary owner exists, the component is escalated to RTAB for ownership resolution
RTAB may assign ownership to another organization, open it to community volunteers, or initiate deprecation if no owner is found
A component is considered orphaned when:
Primary and secondary owner are both unavailable
No PR reviews have occurred in two consecutive release cycles
Health review has not been completed for one year Orphaned components are escalated to RTAB. RTAB must resolve ownership or initiate deprecation within one release cycle.
Every RDK-B component classified as CORE, Required or Optional and is included in reference builds for any RDKB profile that is being released must undergo a health review once per release cycle.
Component builds cleanly on the current reference platform
Test suite is current and passing
No unresolved critical or security defects older than one release cycle
HAL contract is current and matches active vendor implementations
TR-181 data model scope is accurate and agrees with run-time auto-discovery
Registry entry is up to date
No known community-reported regressions are unaddressed

rows: Healthy
No action required. Registry updated with review date.
At Risk
Owner must submit a remediation plan within 30 days.
Unhealthy
Escalated to RTAB. RTAB decides: remediation, ownership transfer, or deprecation.

blocks.text: RTAB reviews all At Risk and Unhealthy outcomes
A component may be deprecated when:
Functionality is superseded by a newer component
Component cannot meet architecture standards and remediation is not feasible
No active owner can be identified
RTAB determines the component no longer aligns with RDK-B goals Deprecation requires:
Migration path defined before deprecation is declared
Operator notification published in release notes
Minimum one full release cycle between Deprecated state and Removed state
Step-by-step migration guide for operators and integrators
Support period during coexistence (deprecated component + replacement)
Test coverage for the migration path
When a deprecated component owns a HAL contract:
HAL contract must be transferred to the replacement component (if any) before removal
HAL contract version must be incremented
Vendor re-validation must be required against the new contract owner
Transition period must be defined allowing vendors to update implementations
When a deprecated component owns TR-181 parameters:
Parameters must be transferred to the replacement component (if any)
Data model backward compatibility must be maintained during the transition period
Breaking data model changes require RTAB approval and operator notification
A component can move to Removed state only when:
Migration path is confirmed complete by at least one reference platform
Repository is archived and marked as removed in registry
Every HAL interface and RBUS API must carry an explicit stability tag.

rows: Experimental
Interface is under active design. Breaking changes may occur without notice. Not for production use.
Stable
Interface is production ready. Breaking changes require RTAB approval and versioning.
Frozen
Interface will not change. Only bug fixes to documentation or behavior clarifications permitted.
Deprecated
Interface is scheduled for removal. Migration path is defined. No new consumers should adopt it.

blocks.text: All HAL headers must carry a stability tag in the file header comment
All RBUS APIs must carry a stability tag in the API documentation
Tag changes must be reviewed by the architecture owner
Downgrade from Stable to Experimental is not permitted without RTAB approval
Interface freeze requires architecture owner declaration and registry update
Unfreeze (Frozen → Stable) requires RTAB approval and a versioning increment
Frozen interfaces that need behavioral change must be versioned as a new interface, not modified in place
For every release cycle, the component owner must confirm:
TR-181 provider list and details are accurate
